name: order_block_entry_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Order Blocks (OBs) are the last opposite-direction candle before a strong impulse move — theoretically marking where institutional orders were placed. Fair Value Gaps (FVGs) are three-candle patterns where the wick of candle 1 doesn't overlap with the wick of candle 3, creating an 'unfilled' price gap that price tends to revisit. In Indian 1-min intraday charts, OBs and FVGs identify zones where institutional algorithmic orders created supply/demand imbalances. When price returns to these zones, the remaining unfilled orders provide support (bullish OB) or resistance (bearish OB). The inefficiency exists because: (1) OB/FVG analysis (ICT methodology) is popular among forex retail traders but barely adopted in Indian equity markets, (2) identifying OBs requires tracking every candle's relationship to subsequent impulses, which is computationally intensive, (3) the zones are specific enough to provide precise entry levels with tight stops.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents + NIFTY 50 / BANK NIFTY index

indicators.name: bullish_OB
indicators.formula: last bearish candle (close < open) before a bullish impulse of > 10 bps within next 3 bars. OB zone = [low, high] of that bearish candle.

indicators.name: bearish_OB
indicators.formula: last bullish candle (close > open) before a bearish impulse of > 10 bps within next 3 bars. OB zone = [low, high] of that bullish candle.

indicators.name: bullish_FVG
indicators.formula: gap where candle[0].high < candle[2].low (3-bar pattern with upward gap). FVG zone = [candle[0].high, candle[2].low]

indicators.name: bearish_FVG
indicators.formula: gap where candle[0].low > candle[2].high (3-bar pattern with downward gap). FVG zone = [candle[2].high, candle[0].low]

indicators.name: zone_revisit
indicators.formula: 1 if current close enters a previously identified OB or FVG zone for the first time

conditions: zone_revisit == 1 for a bullish OB or bullish FVG
close enters the OB/FVG zone from above (pullback into demand zone)
overall intraday trend is bullish (close > VWAP)
zone is less than 60 bars old (fresh zone)
long.confirmation: bullish engulfing candle or hammer at the zone boundary

conditions: zone_revisit == 1 for a bearish OB or bearish FVG
close enters the OB/FVG zone from below (rally into supply zone)
overall intraday trend is bearish (close < VWAP)
zone is less than 60 bars old
short.confirmation: bearish engulfing candle or shooting star at the zone boundary

exit.target: re-test of the impulse move high (bullish OB) or low (bearish OB) that created the zone
exit.stop_loss: 2 bps beyond the far edge of the OB/FVG zone (zone fully breached = invalidated)
exit.signal_exit: close breaks through the OB/FVG zone entirely (zone failed to hold)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22 (zones are more reliable in moderate volatility)
filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: impulse move that created the OB/FVG had volume > 1.3x SMA(volume, 20)
filters.trend_filter: trade OBs in direction of VWAP trend (bullish OBs when above VWAP, bearish below)
filters.event_filter: skip on major news days (zones from before the news are invalidated)
other_filters: only use zones that haven't been revisited yet (first touch only)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — ICT methodology is gaining popularity on YouTube/social media in India but is still niche compared to traditional technical analysis. As adoption grows, OB/FVG zones may become self-defeating (too many limit orders at the zone).

weaknesses: Order Block theory assumes institutional orders create identifiable candle patterns, but in reality, institutional algorithms distribute orders across many candles, not concentrated in one.
FVGs on 1-min bars are common (hundreds per session) — without strict filtering, the signal-to-noise ratio is very low. The age limit (60 bars) and volume filter help but don't fully solve this.
The 'first touch only' rule means zones can only be traded once. If the first touch results in a loss, the zone is removed, even if the second touch would have worked.
prior_art: Inner Circle Trader (ICT) methodology (Michael Huddleston) — popularized OB/FVG concepts in forex. Wyckoff (1931) 'The Richard D. Wyckoff Method of Trading and Investing in Stocks' for supply/demand zone theory. In India, ICT methodology is taught by several YouTube channels but formal academic validation is lacking.
notes: OB identification is retrospective (you see the OB only after the impulse move). This is fine because we trade the REVISIT, not the initial impulse. Maintain a rolling list of active OB and FVG zones (max 60 bars old) for each monitored stock. When price approaches any active zone, trigger the zone_revisit signal.
